briefs.headline: Alonso keeps faith in Penders and names him to start at Anfield
briefs.summary: Xabi Alonso confirmed on Monday that Mike Penders will start Wednesday's Carabao Cup fourth-round match at Liverpool, 4 p.m. ET at Anfield, two days after the 21-year-old goalkeeper punched a corner into his own net in Chelsea's 2-0 home loss to Tottenham, his first Premier League start. "It's part of the business; you need to deal with mistakes and we keep confidence in Mike," Alonso told the club's website. "We win and we lose together." Maxence Lacroix said the squad is "behind him" and called Wednesday "a big game for us. We want to go far in this competition." Cole Palmer serves his one-match ban for Saturday's red card at Anfield and is due back for Manchester United's visit to Stamford Bridge on Saturday at 8:30 a.m. ET. Chelsea remain 5th in the Premier League, two points behind Liverpool.

briefs.headline: Van Dijk says Liverpool's new forwards must now deliver every three days
briefs.summary: Virgil van Dijk said Monday that nobody can replicate what Mohamed Salah did for Liverpool but that the forwards who replaced him "have to step up," after the 2-0 win over Brighton on Sunday, the first match in which Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo looked settled together. "At a club like Liverpool you have to do it every three or four days," the captain said. "I'm pretty confident that it is going to be fine." Isak has scored in six straight league matches; Salah has 10 goals in 10 for Trabzonspor. Van Dijk also praised 21-year-old center back Jeremy Jacquet, signed from Rennes. Liverpool, 4th in the Premier League with four clean sheets, host Chelsea in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Wednesday at 4 p.m. ET and Arsenal in the league on Sunday at 11:30 a.m. ET. There was no update Monday on Wirtz, who went off in the 65th minute Sunday.

briefs.headline: Kane thanks Tottenham as he becomes the first English Ballon d'Or winner since 2001
briefs.summary: Harry Kane, who joined Tottenham at 11 and left for Bayern Munich in 2023 as the club's record scorer, used his acceptance speech at Monday's Ballon d'Or ceremony in London to thank his former club. "I wouldn't be where I am today without Tottenham, for sure," Kane said. "All the guidance, the coaches, you allowed me to live my dream." He singled out Chris Ramsey, Tim Sherwood and Ryan Mason among the coaches who worked with him at Spurs. Kane, 33, beat Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the award and is the first Englishman to win it since Michael Owen in 2001 and the fifth overall; he captained England to third place at the 2026 World Cup. Wembley lit its arch gold afterward. Tottenham, 14th in the Premier League, host Crystal Palace on Saturday at 1:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Bengals safety Dugger is out for Sunday's game against the Titans
briefs.summary: Kyle Dugger, hurt in Sunday's 35-13 win at Baltimore and unable to return, will not play when Cincinnati hosts Tennessee on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reported Monday, per ESPN's injury page, which lists the 30-year-old safety with a left quadriceps injury and describes him as week-to-week; he has played mainly on special teams. Tight end Erick All Jr. was ruled out of the Baltimore game in the second half with a knee injury and had no update Monday. The Bengals, 4-2 and third in the AFC North, half a game behind Cleveland and Pittsburgh, practice Wednesday and publish their first injury report of the week that afternoon.

briefs.headline: Browns activate Gabriel from injured reserve and carry 4 quarterbacks
briefs.summary: Cleveland activated Dillon Gabriel from injured reserve Monday, a day after Sunday's 27-24 win at Tennessee, putting four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster: Deshaun Watson, who has started all seven games, backup Shedeur Sanders, rookie Taylen Green and Gabriel, a 2025 third-round pick who went on IR with a back injury at the August cutdown. Gabriel started six games as a rookie and threw for 937 yards and seven touchdowns. Coach Todd Monken called Sunday "the most complete game" of the season after Watson's first 300-yard day with the Browns and a season-high 491 yards of offense, but the 5-2 Browns have a minus-13 point differential and ESPN Analytics gives them a 5.5 percent chance to win the AFC North. They visit Pittsburgh on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET, where they have lost 22 straight regular-season games since 2003. Defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. is listed out with an ankle injury.

briefs.headline: Brewers rout Rays 10-1 with an eight-run fifth, one win from a first title
briefs.summary: Milwaukee scored a World Series-record eight two-out runs in the fifth inning Monday night at Tropicana Field, seven straight hits, and leads the Series three games to none. Jackson Chourio went 4 for 5 with a double and a stolen base, Brice Turang's two-run single off Cam Booser opened the barrage after Freddy Peralta left with the bases loaded, and Cooper Pratt and Sal Frelick doubled in three more; the Brewers had 16 hits, none of them home runs. Rookie left-hander Robert Gasser allowed one hit and faced the minimum through six innings, the first World Series starter to do so since Curt Schilling in 2001, and Brandon Woodruff pitched the ninth in his first appearance since July 4. Only the 2004 Red Sox have come back from three games down in a best-of-seven. Game 4 is Tuesday at 8 p.m. ET on Fox, Griffin Jax starting for Tampa Bay; Milwaukee had not named a starter.

briefs.headline: Cowboys beat Eagles 38-21 on Williams' 155 yards; Philadelphia drops fifth straight
briefs.summary: Dak Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns, two of them to CeeDee Lamb, and Javonte Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards and a score on Monday night in Philadelphia. Dallas trailed by one late in the third quarter before Lamb's 16-yard catch and Prescott's two-point run, and DeMarvion Overshown's interception of Tanner McKee, in his first game since a Week 1 hamstring injury, sealed it. Dallas gained 416 yards, 204 of them rushing. The Eagles, without Jalen Hurts, who is expected to miss the season with blood clots in his lungs, have lost five in a row for the first time since 2016 and have allowed at least 375 yards in each. Dallas has three wins and four losses and is the only NFC East team with two division wins; the Giants lead at four wins, two losses and a tie. Philadelphia, two and five, visits Washington on Sunday night.

briefs.headline: Cavaliers end Minnesota's unbeaten start in overtime as three teams reach four wins
briefs.summary: Donovan Mitchell scored 26 points, five of them in overtime, and Cleveland beat the Timberwolves 127 to 125 on Monday despite 47 from Anthony Edwards; Meleek Thomas, the 34th pick in June, scored 16 in his debut. Oklahoma City, Houston and Memphis each won a fourth straight to open the season, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Ajay Mitchell leading the Thunder past Phoenix 125 to 114 and Alperen Sengun scoring 29 as the Rockets beat Atlanta 120 to 110; the idle Pistons and Lakers are three and none. Cooper Flagg had 29 points and 11 assists and blocked Andrew Wiggins' late 3-point try as Dallas beat Miami 113 to 109, leaving the Heat winless in four despite Giannis Antetokounmpo's first triple-double for them. Brandon Miller scored a career-high 39 in Charlotte's win over Washington, and Golden State got its first win, 134 to 114 in Denver, on 31 from Yaxel Lendeborg.

briefs.headline: Oregon rules out Moore for the season; Baylor and NC State turn to interim coaches
briefs.summary: Dan Lanning said Monday that quarterback Dante Moore, concussed by a late hit at USC on Sept. 26 and out for three games since, has not been cleared and is not expected to play again this season; Moore had nine touchdown passes and no interceptions in four games, and Oregon has scored under 20 points in every game without him. Lanning fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday after the loss at Illinois and named quarterbacks coach Jay Johnson the playcaller. Baylor fired Dave Aranda on Sunday with a record of 40 wins and 40 losses over six and a half seasons and made first-year defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman interim coach; athletic director Doug McNamee wrote Monday that a hire is unlikely before December. NC State, which fired Dave Doeren on Saturday after 14 seasons, introduced running backs coach Todd Goebbel as interim Monday.

briefs.headline: Manchester United weigh Carrick's future after two days of talks at Carrington
briefs.summary: Michael Carrick arrived early at the training ground Tuesday with no decision announced after talks Monday with chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox that followed Sunday's three-goal home loss to Bournemouth, ESPN reported. United have won two of 12 matches in all competitions, are without a win in eight, and their seven points from eight league matches are the club's worst start since 1986. Sources told ESPN that Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are potential replacements. Carrick, who took over from Ruben Amorim in January and signed a two-year deal five months ago, said after the Bournemouth match that he did not expect to lose his job.

briefs.headline: Carabao Cup fourth round opens Tuesday with Arsenal at Fleetwood Town
briefs.summary: League leaders Arsenal visit League Two Fleetwood Town at 4 p.m. ET at Highbury Stadium, and Bradford City host Peterborough United at 3:45 p.m. at Valley Parade, the two Tuesday ties of the round of 16. Wednesday brings five more: Manchester City against Brighton at 3:30 p.m., Bournemouth against Aston Villa, Fulham against Crystal Palace and Sunderland against Brentford at 3:45, and Chelsea at Liverpool at 4 p.m.; Everton host Newcastle on Thursday at 3:45. Newcastle are the holders.

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu says he intends to compete in Kyushu after 15 bouts on his repaired knee
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu, 27, took 15 bouts against makushita (third-division) and lower wrestlers at the Tatsunami stable's lodging in Itoshima, Fukuoka, on Tuesday, winning 13, in his first practice since the banzuke (rankings) came out, Nikkan Sports reported. He had right knee surgery in late July and sat out all of September; the knee was taped and in a brace. "I am working with the intention of competing," he said of the Kyushu basho (tournament), which opens Nov. 8 at the Fukuoka Kokusai Center, 12 days out, adding that he would not know until the last minute, would decide with his stablemaster and wanted above all not to make it worse. Sports Hochi quoted him saying the knee is improving day by day; he joined the autumn jungyo (regional tour) partway through and stayed to its Oct. 25 close. The Japan Sumo Association's kyujo (absence) page lists no withdrawals.

prime.item: Day 13. Proclamation SF-1-2026, issued Oct. 2 by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler, made the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation; as the Oct. 22 desk read it, the limit for unlicensed persons and harvesters taking oysters for personal consumption is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, with a three-inch minimum shell length, no taking between sunset and sunrise, and the oyster sanctuaries of rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 closed. The division's proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:46 and 5:47 a.m. this morning, lists SF-1-2026 as issued Oct. 2 and effective at sunrise Oct. 15 and carries no later shellfish proclamation. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened at 5:46 a.m., still carries the Sept. 2 table with its oyster row reading season closed, while its footnote (I) reads that oyster season is Oct. 15 to March 31 unless closed earlier by proclamation; the proclamation controls. The proclamation PDF itself was not re-opened today. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:46 a.m. and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, with the footnote that it is unlawful to possess red drum over 27 inches or to gig, spear or gaff them. The proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:46 and 5:47 a.m., carries no 2026 recreational red drum proclamation; the newest proclamation listed by issue date is still FF-47-2026 of Friday, Oct. 23, a commercial flounder order that took effect at 12:01 a.m. today, and nothing is listed as issued Oct. 24, 25, 26 or 27. The reference calendar's October pattern has red drum running and its November pattern leads with them. The reference seasonal calendar, not a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report, published Oct. 1, is 25.9 days old this morning and past the 21-day gate, and no November report has posted.

prime.dates: Open; 14- to 20-inch slot, one over 26 inches
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists spotted seatrout, the speckled trout, at a 14- to 20-inch total-length slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three per day; the proclamations index read at 5:46 and 5:47 a.m. carries no seatrout proclamation issued since the July 1 harvest opening. The reference calendar lists trout for October and speckled trout as prime in November, six days away; Beaufort's thermometer, 60 miles up the coast, read 64.4F this morning, up seven-tenths of a degree from Monday's edition. The reference seasonal calendar, not a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report, published Oct. 1, is 25.9 days old this morning and past the 21-day gate, and no November report has posted.

prime.species: Spanish mackerel, king mackerel and bluefish
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists Spanish mackerel at 12 inches fork length and 15 per day, king mackerel at 24 inches fork length and three per day, and bluefish with no minimum size and five per day, seven per day on a for-hire vessel by the page's footnote. The proclamations index read at 5:46 and 5:47 a.m. carries nothing on mackerel or bluefish issued in October; the two Oct. 20 orders, FF-45-2026 and FF-46-2026, effective Wednesday, are snapper-grouper measures on gag and black grouper vessel limits and black sea bass pot stowage, nothing that touches the sound. The reference calendar lists bluefish for October and November; Monday's Rip Current Statement and Small Craft Advisory have both run out, and NWS Wilmington has only a Coastal Flood Advisory on the beach this morning, below. The reference seasonal calendar, not a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report, published Oct. 1, is 25.9 days old this morning and past the 21-day gate, and no November report has posted.

NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists black drum at a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day, with one over 25 inches allowed, sheepshead at 14 inches total length, five per day, and spot with no minimum size and 50 per day; the proclamations index read at 5:46 and 5:47 a.m. carries nothing on any of the three issued in October. The reference calendar lists October as the peak of the spot run with black drum running, and spot and red drum carrying into November. The reference seasonal calendar, not a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report, published Oct. 1, is 25.9 days old this morning and past the 21-day gate, and no November report has posted.

prime.dates: Harvest Sept. 1 to 14 only; closed since Sept. 15
prime.item: Closed, the 43rd day. NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:46 a.m., reads flounder, all species, Sept. 1 to 14 open and Sept. 15 to 30 closed, unlawful to possess, and carries no October opening; the proclamation behind it, FF-27-2026, issued June 3 and effective Sept. 1 as the index lists it, makes it unlawful to possess flounder for recreational purposes except from 12:01 a.m. Sept. 1 until 11:59 p.m. Sept. 14, 2026, as the Oct. 22 desk read it, and sets no later season. The newest flounder proclamation on the index, FF-47-2026, issued Friday, Oct. 23, is a COMMERCIAL order that took effect at 12:01 a.m. today: as Monday's desk read it with pdftotext, it opens the Atlantic Ocean commercial flounder season for trawls with a 30,000-pound trip limit, superseding FF-38-2026, and closes by proclamation when the quota is reached or at 6 p.m. Dec. 31; it is not a recreational opening, and there is none. FF-44-2026 of Oct. 15 and FF-42-2026 and FF-43-2026 of Oct. 6 and 13, also on the index, are commercial trip-limit and area orders. Flounder in Topsail Sound are release only. The reference seasonal calendar, not a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report, published Oct. 1, is 25.9 days old this morning and past the 21-day gate, and no November report has posted.

going_out.item: Day 4, closes Saturday. The wild boar gun season opened Saturday, Oct. 24, and runs through Saturday, Oct. 31, four days from today, with a second window Feb. 5 to 7; the table's line reads season limit one, electronic registration required. The table carries no county restriction on the line, but the pamphlet is a summary and the West Virginia Code and the Code of State Rules control. Boar archery and crossbow runs on through Dec. 31 and is carried under Prime. The pamphlet is valid through June 30, 2027, checked against this morning's date.

going_out.item: Closes in 13 days. Sora and Virginia rails run Sept. 1 through Monday, Nov. 9, daily bag 10 and possession 30, footnoted (d), in aggregate, in the summary; shooting hours for rails, snipe and woodcock are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset. Wilson's snipe, which shares the table's block, runs through Dec. 16 and is carried under Prime. The dates are not in the hunting and trapping pamphlet, which says so itself; they were re-read this morning from WVDNR's separate Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary 2026-2027, which fetched through the proxy at 5:46 a.m. (HTTP 200, 1,940,942 bytes) and was opened with pdftotext, and Harvest Information Program registration is required.

waters.reading: 103 cfs, 1.65 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on discharge and on stage against 128 cfs and 1.78 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: Down 9 cfs and 0.05 feet on the day against the USGS trace's 112 cfs and 1.70 feet at 5:15 a.m. Monday, Monday's edition reading, a 10th straight falling morning with the recession still slowing: 208 at 5:15 Thursday and 174 at 6 a.m. Friday as Sunday's edition carried them, 148 Saturday, 128 Sunday, 112 Monday and 103 this morning (34, 26, 20, 16, 9), and the trace shows no rain bump overnight, a steady slide from 105 at midnight to 103 at 2 a.m. and 103 at 5:15. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, "103 cfs - prime wading water.", its band for 100 to 200 cfs, and the river sits 3 cfs above the floor of it; at this rate it is under 100 by Wednesday or Thursday morning and the fetcher's read string changes with it. The fetcher's 128 cfs and 1.78 feet 24h_ago fields match the trace's Sunday 2:45 to 5:45 a.m. points, about 48 hours old, so the 25-cfs drop they imply is two days' worth; the falling flags are right. At 103 and clear after ten days of recession the Williams is the long-leader, small-fly problem the desk's instructions describe, and the thinnest water of the month: the pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the file records as its structure are wadeable across at this flow, most pockets are too thin to hold a fish in daylight, and the fish are stacked in the plunge-pool tail-outs and the deepest runs, where they see the angler and the line before the fly. Caddis, stoneflies and sculpin are the forage the file records, so a 12-foot leader to 6X or 7X with a size 18 to 20 caddis pupa or pheasant tail under a small yarn indicator, or a size 16 elk-hair caddis with a size 20 dropper, fished from downstream up the seams and the plunge-pool tail-outs in the afternoon when the water is warmest; a size 8 to 10 weighted stonefly only in the deepest plunge pools, where the depth hides the approach; and the sculpin pattern, olive or black, swung under the undercut banks at first and last light, the only hours low clear water does not work against it. The Williams River in Pocahontas and Webster counties is on WVDNR's fall trout stocking schedule, code F in the 2026 Fishing Regulations Summary as the Oct. 22 desk read it, one stocking each week for two weeks beginning the third Monday of October, which was Oct. 19; the second week began Monday. WVDNR posts stockings by the end of each business day; its fish-stocking page, opened at 5:46 this morning, fills its stocked-waters table by script from a Google Sheet this desk was not permitted to read, so no delivery to the Williams, the Cranberry or the Summersville tailwater is confirmed this morning. The fetcher carries no Williams water temperature, so none is printed.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.62 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 24.39 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.6 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the pool steady, up 0.23 against its 24.39 comparison point and inside its 0.25-foot band; against the USGS trace's 25.05 at 5 a.m. Monday, Monday's edition reading, the gauge is down 0.43 on the day, outside the band, so on the day the pool is falling and the steady flag does not hold. The trace shows Monday's overnight rise given back: the pool topped at 25.07 at 5:15 a.m. Monday, slid through the day to 24.64 at 8:15 p.m., its low of the day, held between 24.56 and 24.71 overnight and stood at 24.62 at 5 a.m., with Huntington below the dam down 0.40 over the same hours, the pool being let back down after Monday's lift, not a river doing anything on its own; the Williams above showed no rain overnight. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 24.6 the gauge is 2.4 feet under the up-and-pushing line at 27 feet. A pool coming back down a half foot after a lift takes some current off the wing dams, and at normal pool the river fishes the structure and what current it makes rather than the slack: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait on a half-ounce head or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam and along the riprap where the current breaks, slower than Monday with less water moving; a half-ounce blade bait or a jigging spoon on the lock wall's deep edge for the sauger, which the cooling water and a 98-percent moon favor after dark; crawfish are the third forage the file records, so a crawfish-colored jig in the riprap for the smallmouth; and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and flatheads after dark, with the falling water pulling them back to the channel edges. The Corps' Huntington District site was not opened and no lake elevation or release figure is printed.
waters.note: This is the gauge above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, the pool side; the Byrd tailwater is not gauged by USGS and is not printed. KNOWN FETCHER BUG, and this morning the direction is wrong as well as the magnitude: the fetcher's 24.39 comparison point appears in the P3D trace at 5:45 a.m. Sunday, Oct. 25, and at 3:15 p.m. Sunday, both about two days back, not 24 hours; against the trace's 25.05 at 5 a.m. Monday the pool is down 0.43 on the day, outside the 0.25-foot steady band, so the pool is falling on the day and the fetcher's steady flag is a two-day artifact. The fetcher's number and flag are printed as the fetcher's and the comparison-window correction is here.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 25.94 feet at 5 a.m., falling against 26.53 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 25.9 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The fetcher reads the gauge falling, down 0.59 against its 26.53 comparison point, and the flag holds on the day: against the USGS trace's 26.34 at 5 a.m. Monday, Monday's edition reading, the gauge is down 0.40, outside the fetcher's 0.25-foot steady band. The trace shows it rose through Monday morning to 26.53 at 12:15 p.m., its high of the day, which is also the fetcher's comparison figure, then fell 0.56 to 25.97 at 11:15 p.m., touched 25.88 at 2:30 a.m., its low of the three-day trace, and stood at 25.94 at 5 a.m., with Point Pleasant above the dam down 0.43 over the same hours, the dam passing less water than Monday, though the Corps' Huntington District site was not opened and no release figure is printed. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access, and at 25.9 the gauge is 1.1 feet under the 27-foot line between that band and up and pushing, a ninth normal-pool morning and the lowest reading of the three-day trace. A pool coming off below the dam pulls the fish off the shallow rock to the current edges, which is where the structure still holds them: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the riprap, so a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked down the current face of each wing dam rather than the eddy behind it; a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head along the riprap points in low light; a black-and-blue jig for the smallmouth and the drum in the rock; cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and the flatheads after dark, on the deeper edges as the water drops; and the lock wall from the downstream side on a live skipjack for the hybrids when the gates are passing water.
waters.note: This is the gauge below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, not the tailwater. The fetcher's 26.53 comparison point appears in the P3D trace at 5:45 and 6:30 a.m. Sunday, Oct. 25, about two days back, and again at 12:15 p.m. Monday, the Monday high, so it cannot be placed to a single hour; against the trace's 26.34 at 5 a.m. Monday the gauge is down 0.40 on the day, outside the 0.25-foot steady band, so the falling flag holds on the day. The fetcher's number and flag are printed as the fetcher's and the comparison-window correction is here.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 3:35 AM at 0.2 ft, high 9:41 AM at 4.7 ft, low 4:32 PM at 0.4 ft, high 10:00 PM at 3.6 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 2:00 AM at -0.2 ft, high 8:35 AM at 6.2 ft, low 3:00 PM at -0.0 ft, high 8:53 PM at 4.5 ft. Water 64.4F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon waning gibbous, 98% lit, 16.0 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 9:41 AM and 10:00 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Waning gibbous, the day after full: the fetcher's file carries the moon at 98 percent lit and 16.0 days old, the full having fallen at 12:12 a.m. ET Monday by the U.S. Naval Observatory table Monday's edition cited, not re-queried today, and the spring tides are still on the water and only beginning to ease; the tide table has not caught up with the moon yet. The sound at Hampstead bottomed at 0.2 feet at 3:35 a.m., and is on its flood at press time, filling 4.5 feet to a 4.7-foot high at 9:41 a.m., the biggest swing and the highest water of the month's table so far, a tenth above Monday's 4.6; it drains 4.3 feet to a 0.4-foot low at 4:32 p.m., fills 3.2 feet to a 3.6-foot high at 10:00 p.m. and drains toward Wednesday's early low, which falls outside today's table. All four sound events land inside today; nothing carries a spillover tag. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: low 2:00 a.m. at -0.2, high 8:35 a.m. at 6.2, low 3:00 p.m. at -0.0, high 8:53 p.m. at 4.5, a 6.4-foot flood against Monday's 6.1 and the highest surf high of the month's table. Today's lags from the two tables are 66 and 67 minutes on the highs and 95 and 92 minutes on the lows; the lows again lag longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the ebb at the crew's spot past what a flat offset would give. NWS Wilmington has stood the water down to one advisory: a Coastal Flood Advisory for Coastal Pender and Coastal Brunswick counties, issued 1:13 a.m., in effect 7 a.m. to 11 a.m., up to one half foot of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways, down from Monday's one foot, low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks named for minor coastal flooding, which lands on the 9:41 a.m. sound high; the Small Craft Advisory on the coastal waters ran out at 1 a.m. and the Rip Current Statement at 8 p.m. Monday, and at 5:46 a.m. the marine zones AMZ250 and AMZ252 carried no active alert and Coastal Pender carried no rip current line, so the ocean and the inlet are open water again by the service's list, for the first morning since Saturday. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 64.4F at 5:30 a.m., up seven-tenths from Monday's edition reading of 63.7; the fetcher's file gives no reading at Topsail itself. What is running is the reference seasonal calendar, labeled as such and not a live report: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report, published Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, is 25.9 days old this morning and past the paper's 21-day gate, the feed still carried it as its newest item at 5:46 a.m., and no November report has posted. The calendar's October pattern is spot at the peak of the run, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum; its November pattern, six days away, is red drum, speckled trout at their prime, bluefish, spot, sea mullet and blow toads, and a Beaufort thermometer in the mid-60s is the cool-down that pattern turns on. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem, and for the first morning this week the weather is not deciding it: the northeast blow has run out of the advisories, the surf is still the bigger water with a 6.4-foot flood this morning and the inlet on the back side of the full moon still carries a hard ebb, but the oceanfront and the piers are back in play for the bluefish and the spot of the calendar's October, a two-hook bottom rig with bloodworm or shrimp bits off the piers on the moving water either side of the 8:35 a.m. and 8:53 p.m. surf highs, and a Gotcha plug or a metal jig under the birds if bait pods show tight to the beach on the morning flood. In the sound the flood runs to 9:41 a.m. with 4.7 feet over the grass and up the dock pilings, the most water of the month, the flooded-high stage where the drum push into the grass and the dock flats, finger mullet and shrimp the forage the file records, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the flooded grass edges and down the dock lines on the top of the flood, with the advisory's half foot of extra water putting the fish farther back in the grass than the table alone says, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead as the bars go under. The ebb from 9:41 a.m. to 4:32 p.m. is the day's working window, 6 hours 51 minutes of falling water still on a spring swing, 4.3 feet of water and the bait in it pulled out of the marsh; the red drum stage, the last of the fall, is roughly 2:30 to 4:30 p.m., in full daylight, a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the ICWW channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low, and with the wind off the advisories the creek mouths on both shores can be cast, not only the mainland lee. For spot in the sound, the same two-hook bottom rig on the channel edges on the moving water either side of the 4:32 p.m. low. The flood from 4:32 to 10:00 p.m. covers the oyster bars and grass edges again, the same spoon and paddletail program, and dusk falls in the first third of that flood, on the low grass edges and the first of the water coming back over the bars, the trout window the calendar is six days from calling prime: a Spook Jr. or a suspending twitch bait walked over the deeper grass edges and the dock lights in the last hour of light, then a live shrimp under a slip cork in the deeper holes, 15 to 20 feet, on the first of the evening ebb after 10:00 p.m. under a 98-percent moon that will light the water almost as well as Monday's. Slack at 9:41 a.m., 4:32 p.m. and 10:00 p.m. is dead water, and on a spring tide the slack is short. Oysters are in their 13th day open under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. Flounder are release only, the 43rd day; FF-47-2026, which took effect at 12:01 a.m. today, is a commercial ocean trawl order and changes nothing in the sound.
